title: Thou Who Roll’st the Year Around
description: Thou Who Roll’st the Year Around in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Ray Palmer wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 165.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou who roll’st the year a-round, Crowned with mer-cies large and free, Rich Thy gifts to us a-bound, Warm our praise shall rise to Thee.

lines: Thou who roll’st the year around,
Crowned with mercies large and free,
Rich Thy gifts to us abound,
Warm our praise shall rise to Thee.
Kindly to our worship bow,
While our grateful thanks we tell,
That, sustained by Thee, we now
Bid the parting year farewell!
All its numbered days are sped,
All its busy scenes are o’er,
All its joys forever fled,
All its sorrows felt no more.
Mingled with th’ eternal past,
Its remembrance shall decay,
Yet to be revived at last
At the solemn Judgment Day.
All our follies, Lord, forgive!
Cleanse us from each guilty stain;
Let Thy grace within us live
That we spend not years in vain.
Then, when life’s last eve shall come,
Happy spirits, may we fly
To our everlasting home,
To our Father’s house on high!

licence: Public domain: Ray Palmer died in 1887.
credits: Words by Ray Palmer (1808–1887), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
